previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia s/p stem cell transplant, chronic GVHD, diabetes, and prior DVT/PE was admitted for a non-healing left leg ulcer and antibiotic-associated diarrhea. She had sustained a leg injury 22 days prior, and despite oral antibiotics, the wound failed to heal. Diarrhea developed on doxycycline but resolved after discontinuation. On admission, she was started on vancomycin, but it was discontinued on hospital day 2 due to lack of infection signs and negative wound culture. A bedside debridement was performed to remove necrotic tissue impeding healing. IVIG was given for low IgG levels. Her pain was managed with oral hydromorphone, and she was discharged home with wound care instructions, a short course of pain medication, and follow-up planned. Weight loss was attributed to recent poor intake from gastrointestinal symptoms.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you. You were recently admitted 
to ___ after a fall. You were found 
to have a fracture of your sternum (breast bone) and left rib 
fractures. Please follow the below instructions to continue your 
recovery. 

* Your injury caused left 6th rib fracture which can cause 
severe pain and subsequently cause you to take shallow breaths 
because of the pain.
 
* You should take your pain medication as directed to stay ahead 
of the pain otherwise you won't be able to take deep breaths. If 
the pain medication is too sedating take half the dose and 
notify your physician.
 
* Pneumonia is a complication of rib fractures.  In order to 
decrease your risk you must use your incentive spirometer 4 
times every hour while awake.  This will help expand the small 
airways in your lungs and assist in coughing up secretions that 
pool in the lungs.
 
* You will be more comfortable if you use a cough pillow to hold 
against your chest and guard your rib cage while coughing and 
deep breathing.
 
* Symptomatic relief with ice packs or heating pads for short 
periods may ease the pain.
 
* Narcotic pain medication can cause constipation therefore you 
should take a stool softener twice daily and increase your fluid 
and fiber intake if possible.
 
* Do NOT smoke
 
* If your doctor allows, non-steroidal ___ drugs 
are very effective in controlling pain ( ie, Ibuprofen, Motrin, 
Advil, Aleve, Naprosyn) but they have their own set of side 
effects so make sure your doctor approves.
 
* Return to the Emergency Room right away for any acute 
shortness of breath, increased pain or crackling sensation 
around your ribs (crepitus).

HEART AND VASCULATURE: Mild atherosclerotic calcification of the thoracic

PLEURAL SPACES: Trace bilateral pleural effusions.  No pneumothorax.

ABDOMEN: Multiple calcified granulomas are seen within the liver and spleen. 
The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  1.4 x 2.3 cm cystic lesion within

seen within the spleen measuring up to 1.4 cm, which were present on prior
examinations, but remain indeterminate, possibly hemangiomas or lymphangiomas.
There is no evidence of splenic laceration.  A small splenule is visualized. 
Small hypodensity within the superior pole of the right kidney is too small to
characterize, but likely represents a simple cyst.  No other abnormalities
within the partially visualized upper abdomen.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: There is acute mildly angulated comminuted fracture
through the proximal sternum.  There is a moderate amount of surrounding soft
tissue stranding, but no large organized hematoma.  Multiple chronic
nondisplaced rib fractures are seen of the left anterolateral ribs.  There is
also an acute left anterior sixth rib minimally angulated fracture (series 4,
image 152), with subtle contour deformity of the distal portions of the
subjacent left seventh (series 4, image 170), and eighth (series 4, image 193)
ribs likely reflecting recent fractures.  Severe compression deformity of the
T7 vertebral body is unchanged.  There also milder compression deformities of
C7, T2, T4 T11, and L1, which are also unchanged.  No suspicious osseous
abnormality is seen.? Soft tissue nodularity within the upper anterior
abdominal wall likely due to injections.  Coarse calcifications within the
bilateral breasts are noted.

1. Acute mildly angulated comminuted fracture through the proximal sternum.
